requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current
project under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. Subsequent assessments
follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
Each obligation of `requirements.authoring.invocation` is mapped to a marked test below. I did not request implementation source.

- **Selecting one existing requirement or example:**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` authors both a requirement and a named example. It checks the evidence record, the `Subject: <kind> <name>` line in the prompt, and the report.
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` checks that `requirements.absent` fails, that stderr names the subject, and that existing evidence is unchanged.
- **Refresh and reassessment (cited context):**
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` is marked for the invocation. It covers `--missing` as the default and as an explicit flag, `--force`, and `--stdout` implying `--force`.
  - It also covers the `--missing`/`--force` exclusion, repair of invalid evidence, and the skipped-as-current report with no model or configuration.
  - The `--missing` and `--force` combinations are tested for both a named subject and `--all`.
- **Reporting subject, backend, model, evidence destination and usage path on completion:**
  - `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts that stdout starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL` and contains an `Evidence:` line whose path resolves to `evidence/<subject>.json`. It also asserts a `Usage:` line.
  - `fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` asserts the same report fields, and that the `Evidence:` path equals the project evidence file and the `Usage:` path is an existing file.
- **Evidence destination is a path by default and stdout under `--stdout`:** the default case is covered by the two tests above. `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` asserts `Evidence: stdout\n` on stderr.
- **In stdout mode the completion report and diagnostics go to stderr:**
  - `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` parses stdout entirely as evidence JSON with a trailing newline. The subject/backend/model line, `Evidence:` and `Usage:` all appear on stderr. It runs six cases that vary the determination (true, false, FIXME), existing versus absent evidence, and verbose.
  - `fn[missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence]` asserts that stdout is empty in the failure cases, with and without `--stdout`.
- **`--config`:** `fn[an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile]` selects a non-default profile with `--config alternate` and checks the model, key and backend actually used.
- **`-v`/`--verbose`:** `fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` covers both spellings, and `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` covers verbose with stdout.
- **`author-evidence` alias:** it is used as the command in `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]`, the stdout test, the submission test, and the `--all` conflict case. The `--missing` test also runs it against a current record.
- **Nearest workspace configuration:** `fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` is marked and exercises the command.

The assertions are specific, so a regression in any of these behaviors would fail a test. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no untested obligations.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current
project under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. Subsequent assessments
follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST initially assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current on initial selection.
After that selection, {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment` governs each round. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
:::{req} reassessment
After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the
edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.
Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.
Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`.
A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without
editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.
